summary: A satirical feature piece poking fun at the rise of e-learning, covering everything from endless "Next" buttons and chatroom-style campuses to unreliable Wi-Fi, humorless AI professors, mountains of e-homework, multitasking, pajama-bottom webcam fashion and binge-watched lectures. It is built around invented, pun-named students and experts who supply comic quotes. It closes by wondering whether the future of education will be a streamlined utopia or a "Gallery of Electronic Bloopers."
one_line: A humorous satirical article lampooning e-learning culture, from unstable Wi-Fi and AI professors to pajama-clad webcam lectures and binge-watched courses.
key_facts: The article, titled "The Digital Lecture Hall: A Virtual Paradise" (subtitled "or Pixelated Pandemonium?"), is satire under the topic "Local Technology and Innovation".
It claims that since September 2023 more and more institutions have adopted e-learning, calling it "the omnipresent fog we can't seem to disperse".

Dr. Sally Clickbait, a psychologist and author of "Swipe Right for Knowledge", joked in a holographic TEDx talk on September 27, 2024 that fingerprints will morph to fit the learning curve of touch screens.
Jasper Bytes, a virtual graduate with a "Gamers' Point Average", admits he sometimes forgets whether he is in class or on a fan forum discussing wizard politics.
Good Wi-Fi is likened to the Loch Ness Monster, and students make pilgrimages to 'The Library' for stable connections as 2025 approaches.
Lost Signal, a nomadic student, says the search for Wi-Fi is more intense than any final exam, and that watching a lecturer freeze beside a buffering symbol during finals is real panic.
AI professors such as Prof. BeepBoop are knowledgeable but humorless; in October 2023 BeepBoop congratulated a student for debugging a program when the student was complaining about an actual insect.
Robotic tutors need no sleep and can endlessly ask "Could you turn your camera on?" to black screens.
Student Ima Stressed says her e-homework load is like having 500 tabs open in her brain.
Timmy Turnitin asks whether to learn calculus or defeat the Dark Lord in his MMORPG, and the article says people often do both with neither getting proper focus.
Polly Polyester compares seeing classmates' upper halves on webcam to an iceberg, with cartoon-character pajamas below the surface.
Dexter Download, famed for viewing an entire finance course in one day, binge-watches lectures like the fictional Netflix hit 'Stranger Semesters' and dozes off during the fiscal policy chapter.
